final_message:
Both functions are implemented and all 13 tests pass (`python -m pytest`).

- **`slugs/text.py`**: `slugify` lower-cases, spells out the six special letters, strips apostrophes, and turns other non-alphanumeric runs into single hyphens. It cuts at the last whole word that fits, or at `max_length` if the first word is too long. Empty results become `untitled`. It raises `ValueError` when `max_length < 1`.
- **`slugs/unique.py`**: `unique_slug` returns the plain slug if it is free. Otherwise it tries `-2`, `-3`, and so on, cutting the base slug to make room for the suffix and removing any hyphen left at the cut. It raises `ValueError` when `max_length < 8`.

One case the README does not cover: with a very small `max_length`, the suffix can grow until no room is left for any part of the base slug. For `max_length=8` that takes about a million collisions. I made `unique_slug` raise `ValueError` in that case, rather than return a result starting with `-`. Say if you want different behaviour there.

--- a/slugs/text.py
+++ b/slugs/text.py
@@ -1,6 +1,45 @@
 """Turning titles into slugs."""
+
+import re
+import unicodedata
+
+_SPELLED_OUT = {
+    "ß": "ss",
+    "æ": "ae",
+    "œ": "oe",
+    "ø": "o",
+    "ł": "l",
+    "đ": "d",
+}
+_APOSTROPHES = re.compile("['\u2019]")
+_SEPARATORS = re.compile(r"[^a-z0-9]+")
+
+
+def _ascii_letters(text: str) -> str:
+    text = text.lower()
+    text = "".join(_SPELLED_OUT.get(ch, ch) for ch in text)
+    decomposed = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", text)
+    return "".join(ch for ch in decomposed if unicodedata.category(ch) != "Mn")
 
 
 def slugify(text: str, max_length: int = 60) -> str:
     """Return the URL slug of `text`. See README.md for the rules."""
-    raise NotImplementedError
+    if max_length < 1:
+        raise ValueError("max_length must be at least 1")
+
+    text = _APOSTROPHES.sub("", _ascii_letters(text))
+    slug = _SEPARATORS.sub("-", text).strip("-")
+    if not slug:
+        slug = "untitled"
+
+    words = slug.split("-")
+    if len(words[0]) > max_length:
+        return words[0][:max_length]
+
+    result = words[0]
+    for word in words[1:]:
+        candidate = f"{result}-{word}"
+        if len(candidate) > max_length:
+            break
+        result = candidate
+    return result
